title: "hpc"

The `hpc` subcommand is used to configure HPC environments.

## Commands

```
  hpc       Master HPC setup
  hpc git
  hpc scratch
  hpc apptainer
  hpc slurm
  hpc r
```

## Installation

Assuming that the HPC is running on Linux, the following line will install `setupmjr` without requiring `sudo` permission:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/main/install-local.sh | bash
```

Confirm that installation worked by running:

```bash
setupmjr --version
```

If the above does not work, then `setupmjr` may not be on your system `PATH`. In that case, you can add the following line to your shell profile (typically `~/.bashrc`):

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

Then run:

```
source ~/.bashrc
```

At this point, the following should succeed:

```bash
setupmjr --version
```

If not, then the initial installation failed.

## Setup

The following command will configure the HPC environment:

```bash
setupmjr hpc
```

The master command is Linux-only and stops on the first failed setup step. It runs the following sequence:

1. Configure `bash` rc.d, executable paths, and login/profile integration.
2. Configure `zsh` rc.d, executable paths, and login/profile integration.
3. Configure Git and GitHub authentication.
4. Install the HPC scratch configuration.
5. Install the Apptainer helpers.
6. Install the SLURM helpers.
7. Configure R with the normal `setupmjr r` defaults.

In practical terms, `setupmjr hpc` does the following:

- *Helps store large files effectively*: Large files are stored in the `/scratch` space (if available) rather than `/home`, to respect HPC storage policies.
- *Authenticates with Git*: GitHub authentication uses either an existing persistent `gh` login or one protected setupmjr-managed token file for headless/HPC environments.
- *Adds `Apptainer` and SLURM helpers*: If these tools are available, helper scripts are installed to simplify their usage.
- *Configures `radian`*: If you use `radian` as your R terminal, it is configured to work properly on the HPC.

Each feature can also be configured independently via the respective subcommands (`hpc scratch`, `hpc apptainer`, `hpc slurm`, `hpc git`, `hpc r`).

### Setting up Git

To configure Git, run:

```bash
setupmjr hpc git
```

This calls the normal `setupmjr git` setup. Authentication is deliberately suitable for headless HPC use:

- if `gh auth login` has already established durable GitHub CLI authentication, Git is configured with `gh auth setup-git`;
- otherwise setupmjr stores one GitHub token under `~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token`, with private permissions, and configures Git to read it through the standard credential-helper interface.

The token itself is not embedded in shell startup files or Git configuration. Existing active `GH_TOKEN=` assignments left by older setupmjr versions are removed from setupmjr's `login.sh` files during migration.

This credential-helper design is also intended to work with R `gitcreds` and with VS Code Dev Containers' built-in Git credential forwarding. In a Remote SSH -> HPC -> Dev Container workflow, configure authentication on the HPC host first. If a particular Dev Container still fails to reuse the host helper, treat that as a forwarding problem rather than copying a PAT into the repository or container definition.

See [git setup](git.qmd) for the full authentication model and fallback details.

### Using scratch space

HPCs typically have a separate scratch space for storing large files (i.e. `/scratch/$USER`), which is often faster and has different quotas than the home directory.
The `hpc scratch` command helps you configure your environment to use the `/scratch` space effectively.

To set this up, run:

```bash
setupmjr hpc scratch
```

This configures the environment to preferentially use `/scratch` for:

- Apptainer and Singularity images;
- R libraries and `renv` caches.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The master `setupmjr hpc` command configures bash rc.d before installing `~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh`. The standalone `hpc scratch` subcommand only installs that file, so use `setupmjr shell bash rc.d` first if your shell is not already sourcing `~/.bashrc.d`.
:::

### `hpc slurm`

SLURM is a popular program used by HPCs to allocate compute resources. `setupmjr hpc slurm` installs helper scripts into `~/.local/bin`:

- `slurm-sbatch`: submits a SLURM job and records submission details;
- `slurm-sintx`: starts an interactive SLURM session;
- `slurm-squeue`: lists jobs for the current user.

### `hpc apptainer`

`setupmjr hpc apptainer` installs helper scripts for working with Apptainer containers into `~/.local/bin`, including `apptainer-pull`, `apptainer-path`, `apptainer-exists`, `apptainer-run`, and `apptainer-rscript`.

### `hpc r`

To configure R for the HPC environment, run:

```bash
setupmjr hpc r
```

This calls `setupmjr r`, which configures `radian` and `lintr`. You can opt out with `--not-radian` or `--not-lintr`, for example:

```bash
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr
```
